primitives.verbatim_quote: 152 PRINCIPLES OF BEHAVIOR the course of 40 trials involving delays of 30 and 60 seconds respectively, eight albino rats displayed a gain in the choice of the act involving the 30-second delay which extended from 47 per cent (approximately chance) to 76 per cent.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator is the probabilistic discrimination between actions with differing reinforcement delays. The system exhibits a learned preference shift from chance-level performance (47%) to strong dominance (76%) under 30s vs 60s delay. This implies an underlying temporal discounting mechanism where shorter delays yield higher immediate value. The acquisition curve reflects a sigmoidal growth pattern, consistent with standard learning models. The delay difference effect suggests that larger disparities accelerate learning, indicating a non-linear sensitivity to temporal variance. The mathematical structure aligns with exponential decay in uncertainty reduction or inverse power law scaling in reward prediction error signals. The empirical validation across multiple studies (DeCamp, Yoshioka, Grice) supports robustness of the principle. The failure mode occurs when delay differences become negligible, causing minimal behavioral change. The dual nature lies in the interplay between temporal precision and behavioral consistency—higher precision in delay perception leads to faster convergence but also increased sensitivity to noise.
